title: Are Dogs Really Man's Best Friend?
summary: A short 2008 How Stuff Works podcast episode asking whether a dog is really man's best friend. The hosts use the story of Hachiko, the Akita-type dog who waited at Shibuya station in Tokyo for his deceased professor for years, to discuss canine loyalty and whether describing the dog as 'waiting patiently' anthropomorphizes it. They note studies suggesting dogs can display secondary emotions such as jealousy, shame, pride and guilt. The episode also includes a brief ad read for a camera and some office banter.

segments.title: Hachiko's story
segments.summary: The hosts recount Hachiko's life: he walked his professor to and from a Japanese university train station daily for about ten to twelve years. After the professor died at school, Hachiko kept returning to the station, was given to another family, repeatedly escaped to the station, and contracted mange and other diseases. He is now stuffed at the Museum of Nature and Science in Tokyo, and his bones were buried next to his owner.

segments.title: Debate over anthropomorphizing the dog
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether writing that Hachiko 'waited patiently' anthropomorphizes him. They acknowledge the show aims for scientific accuracy but argue his continued waiting, despite illness and treats not being the reason, suggests loyalty. They cite studies showing dogs exhibit secondary emotions such as jealousy, shame, pride and guilt, and conclude the wording was a matter of erring on the side of caution.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts invite listeners to read the article and share feedback by email, followed by a repeated camera ad.
